statement: [B-RD7: the first-level tame range] Let $p\geq5$, and permit arbitrary perfect residue fields of characteristic $p$. For $p=3$, the same assertion with a specified tame defect $m=2$ or $4$ holds: defect $2$ occurs exactly at even $e\geq4$, and defect $4$ occurs at every positive even $e$. No assertion about wild 3-primary inertia is included in the latter statement.

statement: [The corrected Fontaine dictionary] Let $M$ satisfy the manuscript monodromy condition, and assume in addition that $V=T_p(M)\otimes_{\mathbf Z_p}\mathbf Q_p$ is potentially semistable. With \[ D_{\mathrm{cov}}(G)=D_{\mathrm{contra}}(G^D), \] the precise comparison for a good graded group $G$ over a finite extension $L/K$ is \[ D_{\mathrm{cov}}(G_{k_L})[1/p] \simeq D_{\cris,L}(T_pG\otimes\mathbf Q_p)(-1). \tag{B-RD4.1} \] The Tate twist in this formula does not change the inertia trace.

statement: [B-RD21: the remaining wild question is one level] Fix $p=3$ and a positive even absolute ramification index $e$. Put \[ s=v_3(e/2),\qquad L=\lfloor\log_3(e/2)\rfloor, \] and define \begin{align*} N_{\mathrm t} &=1+\min\left(s,\left\lfloor\frac L2\right\rfloor, \left\lfloor\frac{L+s}{4}\right\rfloor\right),\\ N_{\mathrm w} &=1+\min\left(s,\left\lfloor\frac{L+1}{2}\right\rfloor, \left\lfloor\frac{L+s+1}{4}\right\rfloor\right). \end{align*} Then \[ N_{\mathrm t}\leq N(e)\leq N_{\mathrm w} \leq N_{\mathrm t}+1. \tag{B-RD21.1} \] In particular the full answer is already determined whenever $N_{\mathrm t}=N_{\mathrm w}$. A gap occurs precisely when there is an integer $k\geq1$ such that \[ k\leq s\leq2k-1,\qquad L=4k-s-1. \tag{B-RD21.2} \] Then $N_{\mathrm t}=k$ and $N_{\mathrm w}=k+1$, so only existence at level $n=k+1$ remains undecided. For full $9$-torsion, the only indices not decided by these results are \[ e=24,30,42,48. \tag{B-RD21.3} \] At $e=24,30$ an example, if one exists, must have defect twelve; at $e=42,48$ its possible wild defects are six and twelve.

statement: [A universal wild trace invariant] Let $n\geq1$, and let $A\geq1$ be divisible by three. Put \[ d=2\cdot3^{n-1}\left(A+3^n+ \sum_{j=1}^{n-1}2\cdot3^{n-j-1}\min(A,3^{2j})\right). \tag{B-RD26.1} \] There is a good supersingular elliptic curve over a complete DVR $R$ with algebraically closed residue field of characteristic three, absolute ramification index $d$, and full rational $3^n$-torsion, whose primitive torsion parameters have extrema $A,1$. Moreover $R$ and this marked curve admit faithful semilinear actions of the following groups, fixing every marked torsion point: \[ C_3;\qquad C_6\ \text{if }A\text{ is odd};\qquad C_3\rtimes C_4\ \text{if }A\equiv1\pmod4. \] The action on the special fibre is the usual faithful subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}(Y^2=X^3-X)$, and all these actions are trivial on the residue field. The order-four generator acts on $C_3$ by inversion.

statement: [B-RD26: the sharp wild higher-torsion criterion] Let $p=3$, $e$ be a positive even integer, $s=v_3(e/2)$, and $m\in\{3,6,12\}$. An additive elliptic curve with full rational $3^n$-torsion and exact semistability defect $m$ exists over a complete DVR of absolute ramification index $e$ and perfect residue field if and only if \[ s\geq n-1,\qquad e\geq\frac8m\,3^{\max(2n-2,\,4n-4-s)}. \tag{B-RD26.10} \] The fields constructed here have algebraically closed residue field. No finite-residue-field assertion is needed for this existence criterion.

statement: [B-RD27: the complete higher elliptic range] For $p=3$, write $e=2u$, $s=v_3(u)$ and $L=\lfloor\log_3u\rfloor$. The largest level admitting an additive elliptic curve with full rational $3^n$-torsion is \[ N(e)=1+\min\left(s,\left\lfloor\frac{L+1}{2}\right\rfloor, \left\lfloor\frac{L+s+1}{4}\right\rfloor\right). \tag{B-RD27.1} \] Equivalently, existence at level $n$ is exactly \[ v_3(e/2)\geq n-1,\qquad e\geq\frac23\,3^{\max(2n-2,4n-4-v_3(e/2))}. \tag{B-RD27.2} \] Among potentially good elliptic curves, the least positive full torsion level forcing good reduction is $N(e)+1$. In particular full $27$-torsion with additive reduction exists at $e=216$, with exact defect twelve. Together with the already proved tame criterion, these formulas decide the elliptic higher-torsion existence question at every odd prime.

statement: [B-RD28: wild character ambiguity in every higher height] Let $p=3$, let $e$ be a positive even integer, and put \[ s=v_3(e/2),\qquad L=\lfloor\log_3(e/2)\rfloor,\qquad N_{\mathrm w}=1+\min\left\{s, \left\lfloor\frac{L+1}{2}\right\rfloor, \left\lfloor\frac{L+s+1}{4}\right\rfloor\right\}. \] For every height $h\geq2$ there are two height-$h$ BT groups $M,N$ over one complete discretely valued field $K$ of absolute ramification $e$, with perfect residue field and $\mu_3\subset K$, such that both groups acquire good reduction, \[ M[3^{N_{\mathrm w}}]\simeq N[3^{N_{\mathrm w}}], \] and their manuscript characters differ on a prime-to-three inertia element. Consequently the least universal B.4 index, if denoted by $\nu_{\min}(3,e,h)$, satisfies \[ \nu_{\min}(3,e,h)\geq N_{\mathrm w}. \tag{B-RD28.1} \] In particular the lower bounds at $(e,h)=(24,2)$ and $(216,2)$ are respectively two and three.

statement: [Cyclic isogenies and a Tate comparison] Let $K$ be a complete discretely valued field of characteristic zero, let $r\geq2$, and let $E/K$ have a $K$-rational point $P$ of exact order $r$. Put $B=E/\langle P\rangle$. There is a split Tate curve $T_q/K$, with a parameter $q\in K^\times$ of positive valuation, such that $B[r]\simeq T_q[r]$ as finite group schemes over $K$. The generic $p$-divisible group of a Tate curve satisfies the manuscript monodromy condition: its two graded pieces are $\mu_{p^\infty}$ and $\mathbf Q_p/\mathbf Z_p$.

statement: [B-RD29: nine-torsion fails already at $p=3,e=2$] Let $K=\mathbf Q_3(\zeta_3)$, whose absolute ramification is two and whose residue field is $\mathbf F_3$. Define \[ B:\quad y^2-xy+y=x^3-x^2-28x-53, \qquad q=2^5\,3^6=23328, \] and let $T_q/K$ be the split Tate curve with this parameter. Then \[ B[9]\simeq T_q[9], \tag{B-RD29.2} \] but the manuscript characters of $B[3^\infty]$ and $T_q[3^\infty]$ differ on an inertia element of order two in the finite inertia image. The first group is potentially good; the second satisfies the filtration condition with good rank-one graded pieces. Consequently \[ \nu_{\min}(3,2,h)\geq2\qquad(h\geq2). \tag{B-RD29.3} \] The same lower bound holds for every $e\equiv2\pmod4$.

statement: [Norm and prime-to-$3$ characters in the quaternion algebra] For the finite subgroups $H$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:B-RD31-finite}, the reduced norm is trivial whenever $3\mid |H|$. If it is nontrivial, $H$ is cyclic of order $8$. If it is trivial, the possible orders are \[ 1,2,3,4,6,12. \tag{B-RD32.1} \] In the norm-one case the prime-to-$3$ character depends only on the tame quotient order $t\in\{1,2,4\}$, and on a prime-to-$3$ element whose image in that quotient has order $r$ it is \[ r=1:\ 2,\qquad r=2:\ -2,\qquad r=4:\ 0. \tag{B-RD32.2} \] Thus two norm-one special inertia images with the same tame quotient order have identical prime-to-$3$ characters as functions on inertia.

statement: [B-RD32: exact restriction of the two undecided tests] Keep $p=3$, $e_K=2$, $\mu_3\subset K$, and height two. In particular its wild subgroup has order $9$ and the two wild order-three quotients are independent. Consequently $\nu_{\min}(3,2,2)\leq3$ if and only if no $81$-torsion comparison of the two specified kinds has different prime-to-$3$ characters. statement: [The positive-section Tango construction, with its signs fixed] Let $B$ be a smooth projective connected variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic two. Suppose that an effective ample divisor $D$ and a rational function $f$ satisfy the following stronger form of the Tango condition: $df$, divided locally by an equation of $2D$, is a regular nowhere-zero differential. Let $k>2$ be odd, suppose $D=kN$ for an effective divisor $N$, and put $T=\OO_B(D)$. There is a smooth projective connected variety $\widetilde B$ of dimension $\dim B+1$, a morphism $g:\widetilde B\to B$, and a smooth section $E$ of $g$, with the following properties: \begin{enumerate} \item If $\pi:P=\mathbf P_B(V)\to B$ parametrizes quotients of the extension \[ 0\longrightarrow\OO_B\longrightarrow V\longrightarrow T\longrightarrow0 \] defined by $df$, and $E_0$ is its quotient section, there is a finite flat normalized cyclic cover $\psi:\widetilde B\to P$ of degree $k$, with $g=\pi\psi$ and $\psi^*E_0=kE$. \item For every integer $a$, its normalized eigensheaves are \begin{equation} \psi_*\OO_{\widetilde B}(aE) =\bigoplus_{i=0}^{k-1} \OO_P\!\left(\left\lfloor\frac{a-2i}{k}\right\rfloor\right) \otimes\pi^*\OO_B(2iN). \end{equation} \item The divisor $\widetilde D=(k-1)E+g^*N$ is ample and effective, and a rational function $\widetilde f$ on $\widetilde B$ satisfies the same nowhere-zero Tango condition with $\widetilde D$. \item For every prime $\ell\ne2$, pullback identifies $H^1_{\et}(B,\mathbf Q_\ell)$ with $H^1_{\et}(\widetilde B,\mathbf Q_\ell)$. \end{enumerate}

statement: [A first-degree comparison of Hodge, de Rham, and crystalline dimensions] Let $V$ be a smooth projective geometrically connected scheme over a perfect field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. Put \[ \begin{aligned} q(V)&=h^1(V,\OO_V),& h^{1,0}(V)&=h^0(V,\Omega_V^1),\\ b(V)&=\rank_W H^1_{\cris}(V/W),& t(V)&=\dim_k H^2_{\cris}(V/W)[p]. \end{aligned} \] Then $H^1_{\cris}(V/W)$ is free and \begin{equation} q(V)-b(V)\ \leq\ t(V)\ \leq\ q(V)+h^{1,0}(V)-b(V). \end{equation}

statement: [A surface kernel produces integral threefold counterexamples] Let $X$ be a smooth projective connected surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$, and let $A$ be very ample with \[ h^1(X,A^{-1})=a>0. \] Choose $m\geq1$ satisfying \[ a(m-1)>h^0(X,\Omega_X^1). \] Embed $Z=X\times\mathbf P^1$ by the very ample bundle $B=A\boxtimes\OO_{\mathbf P^1}(m)$. For every smooth hyperplane section $Y\in|B|$, both \[ T^2(Z)\longrightarrow T^2(Y),\qquad H^2_{\cris}(Z/W)\longrightarrow H^2_{\cris}(Y/W) \] fail, respectively, to be surjective on torsion and to have torsion-free cokernel. More precisely, \begin{equation} \dim_k T^2(Y)[p]-\dim_k T^2(Z)[p] \ \geq\ a(m-1)-h^0(X,\Omega_X^1)>0. \end{equation} Thus A.1(a) and A.1(b), as assertions for every smooth degree-one section, are false in dimension three.

statement: [Explicit integral counterexamples in every prime] For every prime $p$, take the surface $(S,L)$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:OC-generated-Raynaud}. Set \[ \ell=p+1,\quad q=\ell^2,\quad n=\deg N=\begin{cases}2,&p=2,\\p(p-2),&p\geq3,\end{cases} \qquad g=1+\frac{p\ell n}{2}, \] \[ B_p=g+p+2+\frac{p^3(p+1)n}{2}, \qquad a_i=p\ell-i\quad(0\leq i\leq p), \] and define the positive integer \[ r=\sum_{i=0}^p\left[ (a_i+1)\bigl((q+pi)n+1-g\bigr) +\frac{\ell n\,a_i(a_i+1)}2\right]. \] The $q$th-root cover with one root for every member of a generic basis of $H^0(S,L^q)$ has degree $q^r$ and produces a very ample pair $(X,A)$. Put \[ m=q^r(B_p+r)+2,\qquad Z=X\times\mathbf P^1, \qquad B=A\boxtimes\OO(m). \] For every smooth degree-one hypersurface section $Y$ in this embedding, $H^2_{\cris}(Y/W)[p]$ has strictly larger dimension than $H^2_{\cris}(Z/W)[p]$. Thus A.1(a) and A.1(b) fail in dimension three for every prime.

statement: The distinction between a supplement and a complement is material. The four exceptional groups in \cite[Theorem~2.5]{DetinkoFlanneryHulpke2018} are $\SL_2(\mathbb Z/4)$, $\SL_2(\mathbb Z/9)$, $\SL_3(\mathbb Z/4)$, and $\SL_4(\mathbb Z/4)$. statement: [All plane degrees in characteristic two] Let $k$ be any perfect field of characteristic two, let $U_d$ be the ordinary smooth locus in the projective space of degree-$d$ plane forms, and choose a geometric generic base point $\bar\eta$. Write \[ g=(d-1)(d-2)/2,\qquad V=H^1_{\mathrm{et}}(C_{\bar\eta},\mathbf F_2). \] For $d\ge4$, the images of $\pi_1(U_d\otimes_k\bar k,\bar\eta)$ and $\pi_1(U_d,\bar\eta)$ on $V$ are equal and are \[ \begin{cases} \mathrm{GL}_g(\mathbf F_2),&d\text{ even},\\ \operatorname{Stab}(\ell) \simeq(\mathbf F_2)^{g-1}\rtimes \mathrm{GL}_{g-1}(\mathbf F_2),&d\text{ odd}, \end{cases} \] where $\ell\ne0$ is the canonical covector determined by $\mathcal O_C((d-3)/2)\otimes B_C^{-1}$ in odd degree. The nonzero representation is irreducible exactly in even degree; its determinant is always trivial. In degrees one and two $V=0$; in degree three it has rank one and trivial, hence irreducible, monodromy. Thus there is no threshold after which all plane degrees have full linear or irreducible monodromy.

statement: [A differential subring with an analytically ramified completion] Let $V$ be a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$ with uniformizer $p$, fraction field $K$ and residue field $k$. Put \[ V_0=F\cap V,\qquad R=\{a\in V_0:D(a)\in V_0\}. \] Then $R$ is a one-dimensional noetherian local domain, with fraction field $F$ and residue field $k$. Its normalization is the DVR $V_0$, which has uniformizer $p$ and residue field $k$; both the fraction-field and residue-field extensions induced by $R\subset V_0$ are identities. In particular $R$ is geometrically unibranch. Its normalization is not finite, and the homomorphism \[ R\longrightarrow V[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2), \qquad a\longmapsto a+\epsilon D(a) \tag{C-RD11.1} \] identifies its maximal-ideal completion with $V[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$.

Thus, once the reduced triple is realized, the punctured-completion comparison is an exact condition, with no additional polarization, excellence, or formal-algebraization hypothesis. Theorem~\ref{thm:C-RD11} shows that the first problem can already fail under a) and b). Consequently one cannot replace it by the assumption ``$S$ is reduced''. The theorem above settles the extra condition for nonreduced bases once a reduced realization is specified; it does not assert automatic effectivity of a general unpolarized formal abelian scheme.

statement: [C-RD13: the exact image by formal models and compatible charts] Let $S$ be a locally noetherian scheme, let $T\subset V(p)$ be a closed subset, put $U=S\setminus T$, and fix a triple $(A_U,M,\varphi)$ as in C.1. Choose a coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subset\mathcal O_S$ containing $p$, with $V(\mathcal I)=T$, and put \[ T_r=V(\mathcal I^r)\quad(r\geq1). \] The triple is in the essential image of $F$ if and only if there exist the following data. \begin{enumerate} \item An abelian scheme $A_1/T_1$ and a specified isomorphism $\eta_1:A_1[p^\infty]\simeq M_{T_1}$. For $r\geq1$, let $(A_r,\eta_r)$ be the compatible Serre--Tate liftings of this datum to $T_r$, using $M_{T_r}$. These are determined up to their unique reduction-preserving compatible isomorphisms. \item An affine open cover $S=\bigcup_i V_i$, where $V_i=\Spec R_i$, and, for each $i$, an actual abelian scheme $B_i/\widehat V_i$, with \[ \widehat V_i=\Spec\widehat{R_i}_{I_i},\qquad I_i=\mathcal I(V_i),\qquad \widehat U_i=\widehat V_i\times_SU, \] and compatible identifications $B_i\times_{\widehat V_i}(T_r\cap V_i)\simeq A_r|_{T_r\cap V_i}$. Thus $B_i$ is an algebraization of a specified formal object, rather than an unspecified good model. Its formal BT identifications uniquely give an actual isomorphism \[ \widehat\eta_i:B_i[p^\infty]\simeq M_{\widehat V_i}. \tag{C-RD13.1} \] \item A group-scheme isomorphism \[ \beta_i:B_i|_{\widehat U_i}\ \simeq\ A_U|_{\widehat U_i} \tag{C-RD13.2} \] whose map on BT groups is $\varphi|_{\widehat U_i}\circ\widehat\eta_i|_{\widehat U_i}$. The condition requires an actual abelian-scheme isomorphism on this overlap, and not merely an isomorphism of its BT groups. \item For each $i$, finite open covers \[ B_i=\bigcup_a W_{ia},\qquad A_U|_{U\cap V_i}=\bigcup_a Z_{ia}, \tag{C-RD13.3} \] where $W_{ia}\to\widehat V_i$ and $Z_{ia}\to U\cap V_i$ are quasi-affine, with a common finite index set, and $\beta_i$ identifies $W_{ia}|_{\widehat U_i}$ with $Z_{ia}|_{\widehat U_i}$ for every $a$. Empty members are allowed. \end{enumerate} The ideal and affine cover may be chosen arbitrarily: existence for one such choice is equivalent to existence for every choice. No excellence assumption or finite-normalization assumption occurs. The statement therefore applies in particular under a) and b) of C.1, and on reduced and nonreduced bases alike.

statement: [C-RD14: the exact elliptic criterion] Suppose $A_U$ has relative dimension one and $M$ has height two. In Theorem~\ref{thm:C-RD13}, conditions 2 and 4 may be removed. More explicitly, choose an elliptic scheme $A_1/T_1$ with $A_1[p^\infty]\simeq M_{T_1}$. On each affine completion the Serre--Tate tower has a unique algebraization $B_i$, and the triple extends if and only if these $B_i$ admit the actual overlap isomorphisms (C-RD13.2) respecting the specified BT comparisons. There is no additional ample-class or scheme-atlas condition in relative dimension one.

statement: [Relation to the nilpotent correction] The general criterion retains two distinct effectivity checks: algebraization of the formal Serre--Tate object and a compatible scheme atlas on the open-completion pair. They are explicit conditions on the given triple and auxiliary data away from $S$; neither says that the triple already extends over $S$. Theorem~\ref{thm:C-RD12} is stronger when a reduced realization is already specified: it proves that both checks can then be removed, leaving exactly the additional completed-overlap isomorphism. Corollary~\ref{cor:C-RD14} gives a second situation where both checks disappear. The reduced counterexample C-RD11 and the square-zero counterexample C-RD5 show that the remaining comparison cannot be replaced by reducedness of the local rings.

statement: [A smooth root cover makes a generated polarization very ample] Let $S$ be a smooth projective connected surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$. Let $L$ be ample and generated by global sections, and choose an integer $q>1$, prime to $p$, such that $L^q$ is very ample. Then there is a smooth projective connected surface $X$, a finite flat map $\rho:X\to S$ of degree prime to $p$, and a very ample line bundle $A=\rho^*L$. Moreover $H^1(S,L^{-1})$ is a direct summand of $H^1(X,A^{-1})$.

statement: [An explicit Tango curve with a generated root] For every prime $p$, put \[ h=\begin{cases}8,&p=2,\\p^2-2,&p\geq3,\end{cases} \qquad m=hp-1,\qquad d=(p-1)h-2,\qquad \ell=p+1. \] Let $C$ be the smooth projective model of \[ y^p-y=x^m. \] There is a unique point $P_\infty$ above infinity, and \[ (dx)=pdP_\infty,\qquad 2g(C)-2=pd. \] The positive divisor $D=dP_\infty$ is a Tango divisor. It has the root \[ N=\OO_C\bigl((d/\ell)P_\infty\bigr),\qquad N^\ell=\OO_C(D)=:T, \] and $N$ is generated by global sections. For $p=2$ one has $g=7$ and $N=\OO_C(2P_\infty)$; for odd $p$ one has $d=p(p+1)(p-2)$ and $N=\OO_C(p(p-2)P_\infty)$.

statement: [A generated ample Raynaud polarization with nonvanishing] For every prime $p$, the curve in Lemma~\ref{lem:OC-generated-Tango-root} yields an explicitly specified smooth projective connected surface $S$ and an ample globally generated line bundle $L$ such that \[ H^1(S,L^{-1})\ne0. \] Moreover $L^{(p+1)^2}$ is very ample.

statement: [Full coherent hyperplane restriction fails on smooth surfaces in every characteristic] For every prime $p$, there is a smooth projective connected surface $X\subset\mathbf P^r_k$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p$ and a smooth hyperplane section $Y$ such that \[ \ker\bigl(H^1(X,\OO_X)\longrightarrow H^1(Y,\OO_Y)\bigr)\ne0. \] The construction is given explicitly by the Artin--Schreier curve, Tango extension, cyclic surface, and finite root-cover equations in the preceding results, with root exponent $q=(p+1)^2$.

statement: [The exact coherent degree threshold in characteristic two] In characteristic $2$, the preceding construction can be taken with \[ C:\ y^2+y=x^{15},\qquad g(C)=7,\qquad N=\OO_C(2P_\infty),\qquad \ell=3,\qquad q=9. \] For its Raynaud polarization $L$ one has \[ h^1(S,L^{-1})=1, \qquad H^1(S,L^{-r})=0\quad(r\geq2), \qquad h^0(S,L)=6, \qquad h^0(S,L^9)=556. \] The root cover therefore has degree $9^{556}$ and the displayed sections embed $X$ in $\mathbf P^{561}$. For every smooth degree-$d$ hypersurface section $Y_d$ in this embedding, \[ \dim_k\ker\bigl(H^1(X,\OO_X)\to H^1(Y_d,\OO_{Y_d})\bigr) =\begin{cases}1,&d=1,\\0,&d\geq2.\end{cases} \] Thus this example has an exact degree-one failure and injectivity in every higher degree.

statement: [A cyclic cover converts a negative-cohomology class into a restriction kernel] Let $R$ be a smooth projective geometrically connected $n$-fold over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p$, let $L$ be very ample, and suppose $H^{n-1}(R,L^{-1})\ne0$. Fix an embedding given by a space of sections of $L$. Let $q>1$ be prime to $p$, and choose an ambient homogeneous form $B$ of degree $q$ whose restriction $b$ has smooth zero divisor $D$ on $R$. Form the cyclic cover \[ \pi:X=\operatorname{Spec}_R\! \left(\bigoplus_{j=0}^{q-1}L^{-j}\right)\longrightarrow R, \qquad y^q=b, \] where the products of terms of total index at least $q$ use $b:L^{-q}\to\OO_R$. Then $X$ is smooth projective and connected, $A=\pi^*L$ is very ample, and \[ Y=V(y)\subset X,\qquad y\in H^0(X,A), \] is a smooth hyperplane section. The map \[ H^{n-1}(X,\OO_X)\longrightarrow H^{n-1}(Y,\OO_Y) \] is not injective. It also fails to be injective for every smooth section $V(a y+s)$ with $a\in k^\times$ and $s\in H^0(R,L)$.

statement: [Full coherent restriction fails even for smooth degree-one sections] For every prime $p$ there is a smooth projective connected sixfold $X\subset\mathbf P^r_k$, over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p$, and a smooth hyperplane section $Y$ for which \[ \ker\bigl(H^5(X,\OO_X)\longrightarrow H^5(Y,\OO_Y)\bigr)\ne0. \] In characteristic two the construction below exhibits a one-dimensional nonzero subspace of this kernel. Consequently the unqualified coherent-injectivity assertion in A.1 is false. This statement does not decide the remaining integral crystalline claims A.1(a)--(c), or the separate surface case.

statement: [Degrees and the surviving integral question] In this fixed embedding the failure occurs at degree one, on a nonempty open set of smooth sections. For every $d\geq\max(1,\operatorname{reg}\omega_X)$ coherent restriction is injective by Theorem~\ref{thm:A-high-degree}. At any specified intermediate degree its kernel is exactly the image of the finite-dimensional multiplication map \[ H^5(X,A^{-d})\xrightarrow{\,s\,}H^5(X,\OO_X), \] which can be computed from the displayed finite cyclic algebra and the two projective-bundle sequences. The exact intermediate list for this sixfold is not claimed. The surface question is settled separately by Theorem~\ref{thm:OC-surface-coherent-counterexample} below. The crystalline torsion and saturation obligations remain open outside the proved ranges.

statement: [Uniform negative-twist bounds on the constructed surfaces] For the very ample surface $(X,A)$ constructed in Theorem~\ref{thm:OC-surface-coherent-counterexample} in characteristic $p$, one has \[ H^1(X,A^{-r})=0\quad(r\geq p^2-p),\qquad H^0(X,\Omega_X^1\otimes A^{-r})=0\quad(r\geq p+1). \] In characteristic two these bounds are $r\geq2$ and $r\geq3$, respectively.

statement: [An integral product criterion using the relative de Rham complex] Let $X$ be a smooth projective connected surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$, let $A$ be very ample, and put \[ Z=X\times\mathbf P^1,\qquad B=A\boxtimes\OO(m),\qquad m\geq1. \] For every smooth $Y\in|B^d|$, the integral map $H^2_{\cris}(Z/W)\to H^2_{\cris}(Y/W)$ is injective. If in addition \begin{equation} H^1(X,A^{-jd})=0\quad(j=1,2,3), \qquad H^0(X,\Omega_X^1\otimes A^{-2d})=0, \end{equation} then its cokernel is torsion-free and it identifies the full crystalline degree-two torsion subgroups.

statement: [Exact degrees for the characteristic-two integral product counterexample] Take the characteristic-two surface $(X,A)$ of Corollary~\ref{cor:OC-surface-exact-degrees}, and the fixed threefold embedding \[ m=591\cdot9^{556}+2,\qquad Z=X\times\mathbf P^1, \qquad B=A\boxtimes\OO(m). \] For every smooth degree-$d$ hypersurface section $Y_d$ in this embedding: \begin{enumerate} \item The map $H^2_{\cris}(Z/W)\to H^2_{\cris}(Y_d/W)$ is injective for every $d\geq1$. \item Its cokernel is torsion-free if and only if $d\geq2$. \item Its map on the full crystalline degree-two torsion subgroups is an isomorphism if and only if $d\geq2$. \end{enumerate} Thus the exact degree range requested in A.1(a) and A.1(b) is determined for this counterexample.

statement: [A uniform degree bound for all-prime product examples] For every prime $p$, the threefold of Corollary~\ref{cor:OC-all-prime-integral-counterexample} has injective integral second-crystalline restriction in every positive degree. Its cokernel is torsion-free and its full torsion groups are identified for every \[ d\geq p^2-p. \] Both latter assertions fail in degree one. At $p=2$ this bound is exact by Theorem~\ref{thm:OC-product-exact-degrees}. No claim about the intervening degrees $2\leq d<p^2-p$ is made for the additional examples at odd primes.

statement: [All degrees, all characteristics] The generic degree-$d$ hypersurface of $\mathbf P^r$ has bijective Frobenius on $H^{r-1}(\mathcal O)$, and its generic stable rank is $h_d$. In particular, for plane curves the generic rank is $g_d=(d-1)(d-2)/2$, and the smallest positivity threshold is $d_0=3$.

statement: [Refutation of full linear monodromy] For every finite field of characteristic two and every odd $d\geq5$, let $\bar\eta$ be a geometric generic point of the ordinary smooth degree-$d$ plane-curve locus $U_d$, and put $V=H^1_{\mathrm{et}}(C_{\bar\eta},\mathbf F_2)$. Both images \[ G_{\mathrm{geom}}=\mathrm{im}\bigl(\pi_1(U_d\otimes\bar k,\bar\eta) \to\mathrm{GL}(V)\bigr),\qquad G_{\mathrm{arith}}=\mathrm{im}\bigl(\pi_1(U_d,\bar\eta) \to\mathrm{GL}(V)\bigr) \] fix a nonzero covector. Consequently both are contained in the proper subgroup \[ \mathrm{Stab}(\ell)\simeq \mathbf F_2^{\,g_d-1}\rtimes\mathrm{GL}_{g_d-1}(\mathbf F_2), \] and $V$ is reducible, with invariant hyperplane $\ker\ell$. There is no integer $d_1(\mathbf P^2)$ for which the proposed full linear geometric or arithmetic monodromy holds for every $d\geq d_1$ in characteristic two.

statement: Let $k$ be a finite field of characteristic $p$. For every $d\geq4$, every nonempty Zariski open $U\subset S_d$, and every $a\in\mathbf F_p$, there exist a finite extension $k'/k$ and a smooth plane curve $C\in U(k')$ of degree $d$ with $\#C(k')\equiv a\pmod p$. For $d=1,2$ the only residue for smooth curves is $1$. For $d=3$, the residues on the ordinary smooth locus are exactly $\mathbf F_p\setminus\{1\}$, and every nonempty open of that locus attains every such residue after a finite extension. Supersingular smooth cubics give residue $1$, so all residues occur among all smooth cubics; the every-open assertion for all residues fails in degree three.

statement: For every $d\geq d_0$, the generic smooth hypersurface section $Y$ of degree $d$ has $\dim E(Y,\mathcal O_Y)_{\mathrm{ss}}>0$. More precisely, for every $d\geq\max\{1,r_\omega-1\}$, its generic rank $f_{X,d}$ satisfies \begin{equation} f_{X,d}\ \geq\ D\binom dn-D\binom d{n-1} -\sum_{m=1}^{n-2}B_m\binom dm-a, \end{equation} where a binomial coefficient with lower index greater than $d$ is zero. Consequently \[ f_{X,d}=\frac{D}{n!}d^n+O_X(d^{n-1})\quad(d\longrightarrow\infty). \]

statement: [The eventual parenthesis of 8.5.8] For the explicit $d_0$ of \eqref{eq:explicit-d0}, every $d\geq d_0$ has the following properties. Every smooth degree-$d$ section $Y$ satisfies \[ \dim E(Y,\mathcal O_Y) =h^0(X,\omega_X\otimes L^d)-h^0(X,\omega_X)>0. \] For every $Y$ in the maximal-stable-rank open $U_d$, the number of $p$-adic unit roots in vanishing cohomology is positive. Thus, on this open and in this stated eventual range, unit-root nonvanishing and the maximal Hodge-level condition $E(Y,\mathcal O_Y)\ne0$ are equivalent. No assumption on crystalline $p$-torsion of $X$ is needed.

statement: Let $G$ be a finite commutative group scheme over a field $k$, and let $Z\to X$ be a $G$-torsor, where $Z$ is a positive dimensional projective complete intersection of dimension at least two and $X$ is smooth and geometrically connected. If $G^D$ is connected, then \[ \operatorname{Pic}_{X/k}^0=G^D. \]

statement: For the fixed smooth projective geometrically connected surface $(X,L)/k$ just constructed, let $r_\omega$ be a regularity bound for its embedded dualizing sheaf, and put $d_* =\max\{1,r_\omega-1\}$. For every $d\geq d_*$ and every smooth section $Y\in|L^d|$, of genus $g_Y$, one has \[ \dim E(Y,\mathcal O_Y)=g_Y-1, \qquad \dim E(Y,\mathcal O_Y)_{\mathrm{ss}} =f_Y\leq g_Y-2, \] where $f_Y$ is the $2$-rank of its Jacobian. statement: [The conductor inclusion for an even contact] Let $C$ be a smooth plane curve of degree $d$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic two, and let $Q$ be a reduced plane curve of degree $s<d$ with $Q\cap C=2D$ as divisors on $C$. Write $\nu:\widetilde Q=\coprod Q_i\to Q$ for the normalization, and write \[ \operatorname{div}(f|_{Q_i})=2A_i+\epsilon_i, \qquad M_i=\mathcal O_{Q_i}(A_i), \] where $f$ defines $C$ and $\epsilon_i$ is the reduced odd-order divisor. It is supported above the singular points of $Q$. Set \[ J=\mathcal I_{D/Q}(s),\qquad L_C=\mathcal O_C(D),\qquad b=d-s. \] Then \begin{equation} h^0(C,L_C)=1+h^0(Q,J), \end{equation} and there is an inclusion \begin{equation} \nu_*\left(\bigoplus_i \omega_{Q_i}\otimes M_i^{-1}(3)\right)\hookrightarrow J. \end{equation} In particular, with $t=\sum_i h^1(Q_i,M_i)$, \begin{equation} h^0(Q,J)\ge t, \qquad t>0\Longrightarrow h^0(Q,J)\ge t+1. \end{equation}

statement: [No lower-degree reduced contact for a generic curve] Fix $d\ge4$ and $0<s<d-3$ in characteristic two. A generic smooth plane curve $C$ of degree $d$ has no reduced plane curve $Q$ of degree $s$ with $Q|C$ even.

statement: [The theta orbits of generic plane curves in characteristic two] Let $d\ge4$, $g=(d-1)(d-2)/2$, and let $C$ be the geometric generic ordinary smooth plane curve of degree $d$ in characteristic two. If $d$ is even, every theta characteristic other than the canonical one $B_C$ has exactly one section, and geometric monodromy is transitive on these $2^g-1$ characteristics. If $d$ is odd, every theta characteristic other than $B_C$ and $\mathcal O_C((d-3)/2)$ has exactly one section, and geometric monodromy is transitive on these $2^g-2$ characteristics. Equivalently, on $V^\vee$ geometric monodromy is transitive on all nonzero vectors in even degree, and on $V^\vee\setminus\{0,v\}$ in odd degree, where $v$ is the distinguished nonzero invariant vector.

statement: For $e\geq n+1$, fix a hyperplane $H\subset\mathbf P^n$. The local system $V_{n,e}$ retains its full geometric monodromy when the restriction of the equation to $H$ is prescribed to be geometric generic. On the parameter space where both the equation and its restriction have invertible Hasse--Witt maps, the joint monodromy image on $V_{n,e}$ and $V_{n-1,e}$ is the product of their two full images.

statement: Assume $1\leq n\leq d-2$. If $p\nmid d$, then $\bigwedge^nW$ is simple as an $S_d$-module. If $p\mid d$, then $A=\bigwedge^nD$ is its unique proper nonzero submodule; both $A$ and the quotient $\bigwedge^{n-1}D$ are simple.

statement: For $n\geq2$ and $d\geq n+2$, the geometric group on $V_{n,d}$ contains commuting rank-one reflections $R_I$, indexed by $(n-1)$-subsets $I\subset\{3,\ldots,d\}$. At the arrangement base point, their negative eigenlines are \[ \left\langle (e_1-e_2)\wedge\bigwedge_{i\in I}e_i\right\rangle, \] and their product is the permutation transposition $(12)$. Here a rank-one reflection has eigenvalue $-1$ once and eigenvalue $1$ on a codimension-one subspace.

statement: For $n\geq2$ and $d\geq n+2$, the geometric monodromy group $G_{n,d}$ is irreducible.

statement: For $n\geq3$ and $d=n+2$, the group $G_{n,d}$ contains $\mathrm{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbf F_p)$.

statement: Suppose the groups for degree $d-1$ in $\mathbf P^n$ and $\mathbf P^{n-1}$ contain their full special linear groups, where $n\geq3$ and $d\geq n+3$. Then $G_{n,d}$ contains $\mathrm{SL}_{h_{n,d}}(\mathbf F_p)$. If in addition the first of these two groups has full determinant, then so does $G_{n,d}$.

statement: There is a family of plane cubics over a strictly henselian smooth trait over $k$ whose special fibre is smooth supersingular, whose Hasse invariant has valuation one, and whose restriction to a fixed line is the constant squarefree binary cubic $g=x_0x_1(x_0-x_1)$. There are also smooth ordinary plane cubics with this same restriction.

statement: For every $n\geq2$, the geometric determinant images in degrees $n+1$ and $n+2$ are the full group $\mathbf F_p^\times$.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Let $p$ be odd, let $k$ be any perfect field of characteristic $p$, and let $n\geq2$. On the ordinary smooth degree-$d$ hypersurface locus in $\mathbf P^n_k$, the geometric and arithmetic monodromy images on $H^{n-1}_{\mathrm{et}}(Y_{\bar\eta},\mathbf F_p)$ are both \[ \mathrm{GL}_{\binom{d-1}{n}}(\mathbf F_p). \] For $d\leq n$ the vector space is zero and the image is trivial. For $d=n+1$ it has rank one and full determinant. For every $d\geq n+2$ it is irreducible with full determinant.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Let $k$ be finite of odd characteristic $p$ and $n\geq2$. For every $d\geq n+2$, every nonempty open in the smooth degree-$d$ hypersurface locus of $\mathbf P^n_k$ contains, over suitable finite extensions of $k$, hypersurfaces with each of the $p$ point-count residues. For $d\leq n$ every smooth hypersurface has residue $1$. For $d=n+1$ the ordinary open misses residue $1$. Thus $d=n+2$ is the exact threshold for the assertion involving every nonempty open.
depends_on: Self-contained proof in the indicated section
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: The geometric monodromy contains, for each $(n-1)$-subset $I\subset\{2,\ldots,m\}$, the transvection \begin{equation} R_I=1+w_I\phi_I,\qquad w_I=\sum_{\substack{a\in\{2,\ldots,m\}\\a\notin I}}b_{I\cup\{a\}}, \quad \phi_I=b_{\{1\}\cup I}^*. \end{equation} It fixes every exterior basis vector except $b_{\{1\}\cup I}$, which it sends to $\sum_{a\notin I}b_{I\cup\{a\}}$. The swaps for different $I$ are independent monodromy elements.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Let $G_0$ be generated by the arrangement permutation group and the swaps of Lemma~\ref{lem:char2-independent-quadric-swaps}. Writing $\ell=\sum_A b_A^*$, one has \[ G_0= \begin{cases} \mathrm{GL}_{h}(\mathbf F_2),&d-n-1\ \text{odd},\\ \operatorname{Stab}_{\mathrm{GL}_h(\mathbf F_2)}(\ell), &d-n-1\ \text{even}. \end{cases} \] In the second case the stabilizer is $\mathbf F_2^{h-1}\rtimes\mathrm{GL}_{h-1}(\mathbf F_2)$.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: If $d\equiv n+1\pmod2$ and $d\geq n+1$, the universal ordinary Hasse--Witt local system has a nowhere-zero invariant $\mathbf F_2$-valued covector, defined over $\mathbf F_2$.
depends_on: Self-contained proof in the indicated section
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Let $k$ be any perfect field of characteristic two and $n\geq2$. Put $h=\binom{d-1}{n}$. The geometric and arithmetic monodromy groups on the ordinary smooth degree-$d$ hypersurface locus of $\mathbf P^n_k$ are: \[ \begin{array}{c|c} \text{degree range}&\text{both monodromy images}\\ \hline d\leq n&1\text{ on the zero vector space}\\ d=n+1&\mathrm{GL}_1(\mathbf F_2)=1\\ d\geq n+2,\ d\equiv n\pmod2&\mathrm{GL}_h(\mathbf F_2)\\ d\geq n+3,\ d\equiv n+1\pmod2& \operatorname{Stab}(\lambda) \simeq\mathbf F_2^{h-1}\rtimes \mathrm{GL}_{h-1}(\mathbf F_2), \end{array} \] where $\lambda$ is the nonzero covector in Lemma~\ref{lem:pn-char2-canonical-covector}. In the last case $\ker\lambda$ is a proper nonzero invariant hyperplane, so the representation is reducible.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: For every finite field $k$, every $n\geq2$, and every $d\geq n+2$, each nonempty open in the smooth degree-$d$ hypersurface parameter space of $\mathbf P^n_k$ contains hypersurfaces, over suitable finite extensions of $k$, with every point-count residue modulo the characteristic. The threshold $n+2$ is exact: for $d\leq n$ the only residue is $1$, and for $d=n+1$ the ordinary open misses $1$.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Let $X\subset\mathbf P^r_k$ be smooth projective of pure dimension $n\geq2$ over an algebraically closed field. Its connected components are denoted $X_1,\ldots,X_c$ and have degrees $D_1,\ldots,D_c$. Fix $e\geq3$ and $m\geq n+1$. Take $m-1$ ordered variable ambient degree-$e$ hypersurfaces and one of degree $e+\rho$, where $0\leq\rho<e$. There is a nonempty open parameter space $S$ on which their restrictions $D_i$ form a simple normal crossing divisor, all positive-dimensional intersections on each $X_j$ are smooth and connected, and all zero-dimensional intersections are reduced. On this space the joint monodromy of the node sets \[ X_j\cap\bigcap_{i\in I}D_i,\qquad 1\leq j\leq c,\quad I\subset\{1,\ldots,m-1\},\quad |I|=n, \] is the full product \[ \prod_{j=1}^c\prod_{|I|=n} S_{N_j}, \qquad N_j=D_j e^n. \tag{6} \] It remains this product after restriction to any nonempty open of $S$.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Let $B$ be a smooth integral scheme over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$, let $\mathcal E$ be a vector bundle on $B$ with a Frobenius-semilinear endomorphism, and let $U\subset B$ be a dense open on which its stable rank is the generic rank $r$. Let $S$ be a smooth connected affine scheme with a morphism $f:S\to B$, such that the pulled-back stable rank is a constant $r_0$. After shrinking $S$ if necessary, the special Lang local system $W$ of rank $r_0$ and any specified finite collection of finite local systems on $S$ occur as representations of one group $H$ which also acts on a generic fibre $V$ of rank $r$. There is an $H$-equivariant inclusion $W\hookrightarrow V$, the image on the specified finite local systems is their full joint image on $S$, and the image on $V$ is a subgroup of the geometric monodromy image of $\mathcal E|_U$.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Let a finite group $H$ act on $\mathbf F_p$-vector spaces $P,V,W,R,Q_0,Q_1$, with exact sequences \[ 0\to R\to P\to M\to0,\qquad 0\to M\to W\to Q_0\to0,\qquad 0\to W\to V\to Q_1\to0. \tag{7} \] Suppose the image on $P$ is the product $A=\prod_{\alpha=1}^t A_{N_\alpha}$ in its direct sum of natural permutation representations, with every $N_\alpha\geq\max(5,p+2)$. Set $c=\dim R+\dim Q_0+\dim Q_1$ and \[ K_p= \begin{cases} 2,&p=2,\\ v_2(p^2-1)+1,&p\text{ odd}. \end{cases} \] If $t>K_pc$, then traces of elements of the image of $H$ on $V$ take every value in $\mathbf F_p$.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: For $d=em+\rho\geq d_{\rm coh}$, with $m\geq n+1$ and $0\leq\rho<e$, the construction of Lemma~\ref{lem:all-X-independent-nodes} and Lemma~\ref{lem:boundary-Lang-finite-part} gives exact sequences of the form (7). Here $P$ is the direct sum of the node permutation spaces excluding the one exceptional degree-$(e+\rho)$ component, so $\dim P=N\binom{m-1}{n}$; $V$ is the generic relative Lang fibre; and \[ \dim R+\dim Q_0^{\rm err}+\dim Q_1^{\rm err} \leq C(m+1)^{n-1}. \tag{12} \] The superscript distinguishes these error spaces from the numerical constant $Q_0$ in (10).
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Let $k$ be a finite field of characteristic $p>0$, let $X\subset\mathbf P^r_k$ be smooth projective connected of dimension $n\geq2$, and define the explicit integer $d_{\rm res}$ by \eqref{eq:all-X-C-bound}. For every $d\geq d_{\rm res}$ and every nonempty open $\mathcal U$ in the degree-$d$ ambient hypersurface parameter space, each $a\in\mathbf F_p$ occurs as \[ \#(X\cap H)(k')\equiv a\pmod p \] for some finite extension $k'/k$ and some $H\in\mathcal U(k')$ with $X\cap H$ smooth. Moreover, traces of the geometric generic relative Hasse--Witt monodromy group take every value in $\mathbf F_p$ in this degree range. Geometric connectedness of $X$ is not required.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Let $k$ be a finite field of characteristic $p$ and let $(X,L)$ be specified by homogeneous equations and its projective embedding. Fix a degree $d$ for which the coherent relative group is the vector bundle of rank $b=h^0(X,\omega_X\otimes L^d)-h^0(X,\omega_X)$ described above; in particular every $d\geq d_{\rm coh}$ is allowed. There is a finite exact algorithm to compute the generic stable rank $r_d$ and equations for a dense open on which that rank is attained. More precisely, take a rational basis of the relative coherent bundle over the parameter function field $K=k(t_1,\ldots,t_M)$, and let $A\in M_b(K)$ be its semilinear Frobenius matrix. With $A^{[p^j]}$ denoting entrywise $p^j$-th powers, one has \begin{equation} r_d=\operatorname{rank}_K \left(A A^{[p]}\cdots A^{[p^{b-1}]}\right). \end{equation} For $b=0$ this rank is zero. The nonvanishing of the maximal nonzero minors of this displayed product gives the maximal-stable-rank open inside the chosen basis chart, after also imposing smoothness.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Proposition~\ref{prop:effective-generic-rank} is an exact algorithm for each specified input. We distinguish it from a closed structural formula for $r_d$ in terms of fixed invariants of $X$, or a uniform description of its defect from coherent dimension as $d$ varies. The latter determination for arbitrary $X$ remains unsettled in this dossier. No claim that the algorithm was executed for every possible input is intended.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic $p$. Let $\mathcal V$ be the rank-$r$ Lang local system of an invertible Frobenius bundle on a nonempty open $U\subset\mathbf P^M_k$, as for the stable relative Hasse--Witt bundle. Choose a rational trivialization of its determinant line and write its Frobenius as $e\mapsto h e$, where $h\in K^\times$ and $K=k(\mathbf P^M)$. Put $N=p-1$ and \begin{equation} g=\gcd\bigl(N,\ v_D(h)\text{ for every prime divisor } D\subset\mathbf P^M_{\bar k}\bigr), \qquad m=N/g. \end{equation} Then $h=c f^g$ for some $f\in K^\times$ and $c\in k^\times$. The geometric determinant image is the unique subgroup of $\mathbf F_p^\times$ of order $m$. The arithmetic determinant image is the unique subgroup of order $m\delta$, where $\delta$ is the order of the class of $c$ in $k^\times/(k^\times)^g$. In particular, for $k=\mathbf F_q$, \begin{equation} \delta=\operatorname{ord}_{\mu_g} \left(c^{(q-1)/g}\right), \qquad |\det G_{\rm arith}|=\frac{p-1}{g}\, \operatorname{ord}_{\mu_g} \left(c^{(q-1)/g}\right). \end{equation} Both determinant images are trivial when $p=2$, or when the local system has rank zero. For finite $k$, factorization of the numerator and denominator of $h$ computes these quantities exactly.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: At a rational point over $\mathbf F_q$ where a determinant basis is regular, the determinant of coherent $q$-Frobenius is $h^{(q-1)/(p-1)}$. On the Lang frame torsor, arithmetic Frobenius acts by its inverse, since $z^q/z=h^{-(q-1)/(p-1)}$. Thus the geometric-Frobenius determinant character is the coherent Frobenius determinant; the arithmetic Frobenius character is its inverse. The subgroup orders in Proposition~\ref{prop:exact-general-determinant-image} are unaffected by this convention.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Let $X/k$ be smooth, projective and geometrically connected, of dimension $n\geq2$, over a perfect field of characteristic two. Let $L=\mathcal O_X(1)$ for the fixed embedding $X\subset\mathbf P^r$. Write $R_I=\operatorname{reg}(\mathcal I_X)$. Suppose that, for some integer $d_*$, there is a line bundle $M_*$ defined over $k$ with \[ M_*^{\otimes2}\simeq\omega_X\otimes L^{d_*}. \] Put $d=d_*+2t$ and $M=M_*\otimes L^t$. Write $F=F_{X/k}:X\to X^{(2)}$ and $\mathcal B=\operatorname{coker}(\mathcal O_{X^{(2)}}\to F_*\mathcal O_X)$. Choose Castelnuovo--Mumford regularities \[ R_M=\operatorname{reg}_L(M_*),\qquad R_B=\operatorname{reg}_{L^{(2)}} (\mathcal B^\vee\otimes M_*^{(2)}), \qquad \kappa=\frac{c_1(\omega_X)c_1(L)^{n-1}}{c_1(L)^n}. \] Assume \begin{equation} t\geq\max\{0,R_M,R_B-1\},\qquad d\geq\max\{d_{\rm coh},R_I-1\},\qquad d>\kappa. \end{equation} On the maximal-stable-rank smooth-hypersurface open $U_d$, the relative Hasse--Witt local system $\mathcal V_d$ has a canonical nonzero morphism \begin{equation} \lambda_M:\mathcal V_d\longrightarrow\mathbf F_2. \end{equation} Here ``canonical'' is relative to the given square root and its isomorphism with $\omega_X L^d$; the construction is described below. In particular, both the geometric and arithmetic images fix a nonzero covector. If $\operatorname{rank}\mathcal V_d\geq2$, they are proper subgroups of $\GL(\mathcal V_{d,\bar\eta})$ and the representation is reducible. If the square root is defined only after an algebraic extension of $k$, the conclusion about the geometric image still holds. There are arbitrarily large degrees satisfying \eqref{eq:adjunction-covector-threshold}; the rank is at least two for all sufficiently large such degrees, by the previously proved explicit stable-rank lower bound (or by the all-residue theorem when $k$ is finite).
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: For $X=\mathbf P^n$ and $L=\mathcal O(1)$, the square-root condition is $d-n-1\equiv0\pmod2$. In homogeneous monomial coordinates the construction recovers the covector whose entry indexed by $u$ is the defining coefficient $c_u$ when all coordinates of $u$ are odd, and zero otherwise. Thus this obstruction is an ambient adjunction phenomenon, rather than a property limited to plane theta characteristics. The theorem gives a subgroup constraint for general $X$, not equality with the full covector stabilizer.
depends_on: Self-contained proof in the indicated section
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Let $A$ be an ordinary abelian variety of dimension $n\geq2$ over a perfect field of characteristic two, with fixed very ample $L=\mathcal O_A(1)$. For every sufficiently large even degree $d=2t$, the geometric monodromy of $\mathcal V_d$ acts trivially on a quotient of dimension $2^n-1$. More precisely, write $F:A\to A^{(2)}$ and, after a field extension splitting $\ker F$, write \[ F_*\mathcal O_A=\bigoplus_{\chi\in H}\mathcal N_\chi, \qquad H=\operatorname{Hom}(\ker F,\mathbf G_m) \simeq(\mathbf Z/2)^n. \] Set \[ R=\max_{\chi\in H} \operatorname{reg}_{L^{(2)}}(\mathcal N_\chi). \] It suffices that $t\geq\max\{1,R\}$ and $2t\geq\max\{d_{\rm coh},\operatorname{reg}(\mathcal I_A)-1\}$. After the same splitting extension, the arithmetic image also fixes this quotient pointwise.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Already for an ordinary abelian surface there is a fixed quotient of dimension three. Thus even the proposed replacement ``full stabilizer of one adjunction covector'' would be too large for general ambient varieties. The proposition gives a lower bound for the full fixed covector space; it does not assert that no further invariants occur, nor determine the whole monodromy group.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Here is a completely specified ambient surface, with an executed ordinary-hypersurface calculation. Over $\mathbf F_2$, let \[ E:\quad Y^2Z+XYZ+X^3+Z^3=0,\qquad A=E\times E,\qquad L=\mathcal O_E(3O)\boxtimes\mathcal O_E(3O), \] where $O=[0:1:0]$, and embed $A$ in $\mathbf P^8$ by the Segre embedding of these two plane cubics. The derivatives of the displayed cubic have no common projective zero on $E$; its four $\mathbf F_2$-points are $[0:1:1],[1:0:1],[1:1:1],O$. Thus $E$ is smooth and ordinary (its Frobenius trace is $-1$). The degree-one section \begin{equation} Z_1Z_2+Z_1Y_2+X_1Y_2+Y_1X_2=0 \end{equation} cuts out a smooth ordinary genus-ten curve on $A$. The exact programs \path{ordinary_abelian_surface.py} and \path{ordinary_abelian_degree_one.py}, with their retained JSON outputs, verify this as follows. On $E\setminus\{O\}$ write $x=X/Z,y=Y/Z$ and $\omega=dx/x$. The coefficient Cartier map satisfies \[ T(x^{2a})=x^a,\quad T(x^{2a+1})=0,\quad T(x^{2a}y)=x^{a+1},\quad T(x^{2a+1}y)=x^a(y+1). \] These formulas follow directly from $((y+1)/x)^2=y/x+x$ and the decomposition $k(E)=k(E)^2\oplus xk(E)^2$. Multiplication uses $y^2=x^3+xy+1$. On the tensor basis $(1,x,y)\otimes(1,x,y)$ the Cartier map $g\mapsto T_1T_2(sg)$ has the following nine columns, encoded as binary integers from the first basis vector: \[ (3,21,46,16,170,357,154,493,116). \] Its rank over $\mathbf F_2$ is nine. Quotienting the fixed line $ks$ gives relative rank eight. Together with the ordinary ambient $H^1(A,\mathcal O_A)$ of rank two, this proves $p$-rank ten. Smoothness is checked on all four product charts $Z_i\ne0$ or $Y_i\ne0$. The invariant tangent vector field has components $(x,x^2+y)$ on the first chart and $(1+u+v^2,u^2+v)$ on $u=X/Y,v=Z/Y$. On each product chart the ideal generated by the two elliptic equations, the section, and its two tangent derivatives has Groebner basis $[1]$ over $\mathbf F_2$. These charts cover $A$ and the vector fields never vanish, so these certificates prove smoothness over the algebraic closure. The direct count is eight rational points, consistent with the computed Cartier trace zero. It follows that the generic degree-$d$ section on this \emph{fixed} embedded surface is ordinary for every $d\geq1$. Indeed choose $d$ general ordinary members of $|L|$; they meet transversely, with no triple intersections. Each has genus ten and each pair meets in $L^2=18$ points. Their connected nodal union has \[ h^1(\mathcal O)=10d+18\binom d2-d+1=9d^2+1. \] The normalization sequence expresses this cohomology as an extension of the ordinary component cohomology by the Frobenius-bijective graph cohomology. Its Frobenius is therefore bijective. Openness of that condition and the existence of smooth members give ordinary generic smooth sections. Thus \begin{equation} r_d=9d^2-1\qquad\text{for every }d\geq1. \end{equation} The ambient restriction map is surjective in every degree: restriction of plane forms to each cubic is surjective, and Segre monomials span all forms of bidegree $(d,d)$. For every even $d\geq2$, the four character summands have nonzero spaces of sections (their factors on each elliptic curve have degree $3d/2$), so the fixed quotient of Proposition~\ref{prop:ordinary-abelian-fixed-quotient} has dimension three with no additional degree bound. The degree-two program also gives an explicit smooth ordinary genus-37 section: its 36-dimensional Cartier matrix has rank 36; the relative rank is 35, and its four character covectors have rank four before taking the single relation and rank three afterwards. All defining coefficients, matrix columns, covectors, chart certificates and the count of seven rational points are retained in its JSON output.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Let $E_1,E_2$ be ordinary elliptic curves over a perfect field of characteristic $p$, and let \[ A=E_1\times E_2,\qquad L=\mathcal O_{E_1}(aO_1)\boxtimes\mathcal O_{E_2}(bO_2), \qquad a,b\geq3. \] For every $d\geq1$ with $p\mid ad$ and $p\mid bd$, the geometric relative Hasse--Witt monodromy of smooth members of $|L^d|$ fixes pointwise a quotient of dimension two. The same is true of arithmetic monodromy if both $E_i[p]^{\et}$ are constant over the base field. The statement applies equally to ambient degree-$d$ hypersurfaces for the product embedding by $L$. In particular, over $\mathbf F_3$ take \begin{equation} E:\quad y^2=x^3+x^2+1, \qquad A=E\times E,\qquad L=\mathcal O_E(3O)\boxtimes\mathcal O_E(3O). \end{equation} For this fixed smooth embedded surface, both monodromy images have a fixed quotient of dimension two for \emph{every} $d\geq1$. In particular no eventual full-linear-group assertion holds for this $X$, even in odd characteristic.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Let $E_1,\ldots,E_n$ be ordinary elliptic curves over a perfect field of characteristic $p$, where $n\geq2$, and set \[ X=\prod_{i=1}^nE_i,\qquad L=\boxtimes_{i=1}^n\mathcal O_{E_i}(a_iO_i),\quad a_i\geq3, \qquad h_d=d^n\prod_i a_i. \] Use the product of the indicated complete embeddings and the Segre embedding as the fixed projective embedding of $X$. Then the generic relative Hasse--Witt rank is \begin{equation} r_d=h_d-1\qquad\text{for every }d\geq1. \end{equation} In particular the generic relative coherent Frobenius is invertible in every degree. Suppose in addition that $p\mid a_i d$ for every $i$. For geometric monodromy on its maximal-rank open one has \begin{equation} \dim_{\mathbf F_p}(\mathcal V_{d,\bar\eta}^{\vee})^{G_{\rm geom}} =\begin{cases} 2^n-1,&p=2,\\ n,&p\text{ odd}. \end{cases} \end{equation} After a finite extension splitting the Frobenius kernel and normalizing its invariant top Cartier differential, the arithmetic invariant space is the same space. Thus these numbers give the dimension of the entire trivial quotient, rather than a lower bound for it.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: For the explicit surface over $\mathbf F_3$ in \eqref{eq:odd-product-explicit-elliptic}, the relative rank is $9d^2-1$ and the full geometric and arithmetic invariant covector spaces both have dimension two, for every $d\geq1$. For the surface over $\mathbf F_2$ in Example~\ref{ex:ordinary-abelian-surface-explicit}, the relative rank is also $9d^2-1$, and both invariant covector spaces have dimension three for every even $d\geq2$. The exact full images inside the pointwise stabilizers of these quotients are not determined by this theorem.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Suppose $k=\mathbf F_q$ and the fixed smooth projective embedding $X\subset\mathbf P^m_k$ is given by homogeneous equations. For every \[ d\geq d_{\rm coh}=\max\{1,\operatorname{reg}(\omega_X)-1\}, \] there is an explicit terminating algorithm that outputs, up to a simultaneous choice of basis, the complete finite lists of matrices \[ G_{\rm geom},G_{\rm arith}\subset\GL_{r_d}(\mathbf F_p) \] for the local system in A.4. It also decides geometric and arithmetic irreducibility and outputs the determinant images. The algorithm uses only finite linear algebra, Groebner-basis computations, construction of finite fields, and bounded enumeration of polynomials and matrices. It does not call an oracle for Galois groups or for factorization over an algebraic closure.

statement: The theorem outputs the whole finite group for each specified finite-field input, with a proved finite algorithm. Its worst-case complexity is enormous: even the frame dimension is $|\GL_r(\mathbf F_p)|$. It does not supply a uniform structural description of the groups as $X$ and $d$ vary. Nor does it supply a uniform algorithm for arithmetic monodromy over an arbitrary perfect field presented without effective field operations and factorization data. Those distinctions are retained in the result ledger.

statement: The retained program \path{lang_frame_quartic.py} executes a nontrivial small frame calculation for a genuine smooth plane-quartic family. Over $\mathbf F_2(t)$ take \[ f_t=x^4+y^4+z^4+x^2yz+xz^3+txy^3+xyz^2. \] In the standard genus-three monomial basis its Hasse matrix is \[ A_t=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&0&1\\0&t&1\end{pmatrix}. \] The program extracts these coefficients from $f_t$ and checks that all three affine-chart singularity ideals have Groebner basis $[1]$ over $\mathbf F_2(t)$. Thus the generic curve is smooth and ordinary, since $\det A_t=t\ne0$. The first coordinate is a constant summand. A frame of the remaining rank-two Lang module has columns $(c^2,c)^t$ and $(d^2,d)^t$, with algebra \[ R=\mathbf F_2(t)[c,d]/ \left(c^3+\frac{c+1}{t},\quad d^2+cd+c^2+\frac1t\right). \] Its basis is $1,c,c^2,d,cd,c^2d$, and its frame determinant is $cd(c+d)=1/t$. The program verifies all six substitutions from $\GL_2(\mathbf F_2)$ preserve this algebra. It also finds the primitive element $\theta=c+td$, whose minimal polynomial, after clearing denominators, is \[ t^2 Z^6+(t^3+t^2)Z^3+(t^4+t^2+1)Z^2 +(t^4+t)Z+t^6+t^5+1. \] Linear independence of $1,\theta,\ldots,\theta^5$ and annihilation by this polynomial are checked exactly. Its geometric irreducibility has a direct certificate. The first equation gives $t=(c+1)/c^3$, a separable degree-three map of rational function fields. Setting $u=d/c$ transforms the second equation into \[ u^2+u=\frac1{c+1}. \] The right side has a simple pole and is not an Artin--Schreier coboundary over $\overline{\mathbf F}_2(c)$: every pole of $v^2+v$ has even order. Thus the frame algebra remains a field of degree six after extending constants to the algebraic closure. Both monodromy images of this particular curve family are exactly $\operatorname{diag}(1,\GL_2(\mathbf F_2))\subset\GL_3(\mathbf F_2)$. This is a restricted one-parameter family, not the full space of plane quartics, whose image was determined earlier. Its exact coefficient matrix, basis, six group elements, minimal polynomial and smoothness certificates are retained in \texttt{lang\_frame\_quartic.json}.

statement: Let $k_0$ be a finitely generated field over $\mathbf F_p$, given by a finite field presentation. Arithmetic and factorization of separable univariate polynomials over $k_0(t_1,\ldots,t_M)$ are terminating exact procedures. For a polynomial that defines a finite separable field extension of this rational function field, its absolutely irreducible factors over $\bar k_0(t_1,\ldots,t_M)$ can also be found by a terminating procedure, with their coefficients in explicitly presented finite separable extensions of $k_0$.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: Let $k$ be any perfect field of characteristic $p$, and let the fixed smooth projective embedding $X/k$ be defined over a finitely generated subfield $k_0\subset k$. Fix $d\geq d_{\rm coh}$. There is a terminating construction from a finite presentation of this field of definition and the equations of $X$ of the following finite data: \[ H_{\rm geom}\triangleleft H_0\subset\GL_{r_d}(\mathbf F_p), \qquad E/k_0\text{ finite Galois},\qquad \rho:H_0\twoheadrightarrow\operatorname{Gal}(E/k_0), \quad\ker\rho=H_{\rm geom}. \] The two groups are output as complete lists of matrices, $E$ by a finite field presentation, and $\rho$ by its action on generators of $E$. In a compatible geometric frame, the requested images over $k$ are exactly \begin{equation} G_{\rm geom}=H_{\rm geom},\qquad G_{\rm arith}=\rho^{-1} \bigl(\operatorname{Gal}(E/(E\cap k))\bigr). \end{equation} The intersection is taken using the chosen embedding of $E$ into a separable algebraic closure of $k_0$ inside an algebraic closure of $k$. Changing the initial frame conjugates all the displayed matrix groups simultaneously. Geometric irreducibility is a finite subspace test on $H_{\rm geom}$. Arithmetic irreducibility is the same test on the explicit preimage in \eqref{eq:perfect-field-monodromy-formula}; the only additional base-field information is the finite intersection $E\cap k$.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: The theorem is an exact finite-data description for an arbitrary perfect field, and an algorithm whenever the finite field-of-definition presentation and the finite constant intersection can be evaluated. It makes no claim that membership in an arbitrary unpresented, possibly noncomputable perfect field can be decided by a universal program. For a finite base field, the intersection is computed by finite-field arithmetic and the previous theorem already gives a complete unconditional algorithm. The structural question of identifying these outputs uniformly as familiar finite groups is separate; for projective space it was answered above, whereas for general ambient varieties it is not inferred from this construction.

statement: [A line certificate for generic stable defect one] Let $M(s)$ be a $b\times b$ matrix of homogeneous linear forms over $\mathbf F_2$ in homogeneous coordinates on $P=\mathbf P^m$. Suppose $h(s)=\det M(s)$ is nonzero. Let $a,b_0$ be coefficient vectors with $\det M(b_0)=1$. If, at every root $\alpha$ of $\det M(a+t b_0)$ over $\overline{\mathbf F}_2$, one has \[ \rank\bigl(M(a+\alpha b_0)^{[2]}M(a+\alpha b_0)\bigr)=b-1, \] then at the geometric generic point of every irreducible component of $h=0$ the semilinear map with matrix $M(s)^t$ has stable rank $b-1$.

statement: [Rank-one loss and transvection generation] Let $\mathcal E$ be a vector bundle of rank $r$ on a projective space $P$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic two, with a Frobenius-linear endomorphism. Suppose this map is generically bijective, and at the generic point of every component of its noninvertibility divisor its stable rank is $r-1$. Then the geometric image of the Lang local system on the invertibility open is generated by transvections.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [A small Frobenius certificate for a transvection group] Let $N$ be either $8$ or $32$, and let $H\triangleleft G\subseteq\GL_N(\mathbf F_2)$. Suppose $H$ is nontrivial and generated by transvections, and $G$ contains an element whose characteristic polynomial is irreducible of degree $N$ and is not reciprocal. Then $H=G=\GL_N(\mathbf F_2)$.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [Exact groups in degrees one and two on one fixed surface] Let \[ E:\quad Y^2Z+XYZ+X^3+Z^3=0\quad\text{over }\mathbf F_2, \qquad X=E\times E, \qquad L=\mathcal O_E(3O)\boxtimes\mathcal O_E(3O), \] with the fixed Segre embedding of the two plane cubics. For the relative Hasse--Witt local system on the ordinary smooth degree-$d$ hypersurface-section open, both geometric and arithmetic images are, up to a common choice of basis, \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c} d&\rank\mathcal V_d&G_{\rm geom}=G_{\rm arith}\\ \hline 1&8&\GL_8(\mathbf F_2)\\ 2&35&\left\{ \begin{pmatrix}A&B\\0&I_3\end{pmatrix}: A\in\GL_{32}(\mathbf F_2),\ B\in M_{32\times3}(\mathbf F_2) \right\}. \end{array} \] In particular the second image is the full pointwise stabilizer of the three independent covectors already constructed, of order $2^{96}|\GL_{32}(\mathbf F_2)|$. The same statements hold after base change to any perfect field of characteristic two.

statement: [Verification scope] The group conclusions use the lemmas proved here, the elementary cocycle and socle arguments already proved, and the single opened finite-group classification specified above. The retained program provides exact polynomial, rank and Frobenius certificates. It does not infer monodromy from a random sample. The exploratory search chooses certificates, after which every statement needed from each certificate is verified exactly. The high-dimensional characteristic polynomials are also recomputed independently by SymPy's integer characteristic-polynomial routine and reduced modulo two. No assertion for degree $d\ge3$ on this surface follows just from these two degree calculations.

statement: Let $N\ge4$ and $H\triangleleft G\subseteq\GL_N(\mathbf F_2)$. Suppose that $H$ is nontrivial and generated by transvections. Assume $G$ contains an element $g$ whose characteristic polynomial is irreducible and not reciprocal, and whose order is divisible by a prime $\ell$ with $\operatorname{ord}_{\ell}(2)=N$. Then $H=G=\GL_N(\mathbf F_2)$.

statement: For the fixed surface and embedding in Theorem~\ref{thm:product-char2-two-full-groups}, the geometric and arithmetic groups in degree three are both $\GL_{80}(\mathbf F_2)$, over every perfect extension of $\mathbf F_2$.

statement: [The required jet separation] If $L$ is very ample on a smooth variety, $L^3$ separates second jets at one point and first jets at two distinct points. On a smooth projective surface its complete linear system has an irreducible discriminant whose generic member has exactly one ordinary node; the nonreduced locus has codimension at least two.

statement: [Transvection generation in every degree] For the fixed $X=E\times E$ and $L$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:product-char2-two-full-groups}, every geometric monodromy group $G_{{\rm geom},d}$, $d\ge1$, is generated by transvections. Equivalently for the proof, every geometric irreducible component of the full degree-$d$ Hasse divisor has generic stable rank exactly $9d^2-2$ on the relative coherent bundle of rank $9d^2-1$.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [All characteristic-two invariant covectors on products] Let $X=\prod_{i=1}^n E_i$ be a product of ordinary elliptic curves in characteristic two, $n\ge2$, and $L=\boxtimes_i\mathcal O_{E_i}(a_iO_i)$ with $a_i\ge3$. For any $d\ge1$, let $e=\#\{i: a_i d\text{ is even}\}$. Then the entire geometric invariant covector space has dimension \[ \dim(V_d^\vee)^{G_{{\rm geom},d}}=2^e-1. \] After a finite extension splitting the ordinary Frobenius kernels and normalizing the invariant top Cartier differential, the arithmetic invariant space is the same space. In particular, on the fixed $E\times E$ with $a_1=a_2=3$, this dimension is zero for odd $d$ and three for even $d$.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [What the uniform results leave open] For the fixed surface, we now know the exact generic rank, the entire invariant quotient in every degree, and that geometric monodromy is generated by transvections in every degree. The complete images are identified above in degrees one, two and three. A transvection-generated group with the stated invariant quotient can still have further invariant subspaces or a proper translation subgroup. The two uniform theorems do not remove those possibilities for all $d$, and no all-degree full-stabilizer assertion is made here.

statement: For the fixed surface $E\times E$ and embedding considered above, the full Hasse polynomial $h_d(s)=\det M_d(s)$ is geometrically reduced for every $d\ge1$.

statement: [Frobenius-periodic reflexive sheaves] Let $P$ be projective space over an algebraically closed field of characteristic two. If a coherent reflexive sheaf $\mathcal S$ has an isomorphism $F^*\mathcal S\simeq\mathcal S$, then it is a trivial vector bundle with its constant unit-Frobenius structure.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [Determinant allocation] Let $P=\mathbf P^m$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic two, and let $\mathcal E=\Omega_P^1$ carry a generically invertible Frobenius-linear map. Suppose its Hasse divisor is reduced and irreducible. Every nonzero proper invariant subspace of its Lang representation has trivial quotient representation.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [A fixed natural block in every higher degree] For every $d\ge3$, the geometric group on the fixed surface contains a subgroup acting as the natural $\GL_{80}(\mathbf F_2)$ on an $80$-dimensional direct summand and trivially on a complementary summand.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [Conditional exact uniform product groups] Fix $d\ge3$ on the surface $E\times E$ above. If the degree-$d$ Hasse divisor is geometrically irreducible, then both geometric and arithmetic groups are \[ \begin{cases} \GL_{9d^2-1}(\mathbf F_2),&d\text{ odd},\\ \mathbf F_2^{\,3(9d^2-4)}\rtimes\GL_{9d^2-4}(\mathbf F_2), &d\text{ even}, \end{cases} \] where in the second line the group is the full pointwise stabilizer of the three known independent covectors. Theorem~\ref{thm:product-Hasse-irred} below proves the required geometric irreducibility for every $d\ge4$, thereby completing the entire fixed-surface full-image problem together with the three certified initial degrees.

statement: [Why reducedness alone was insufficient] Generic stable loss one proves reducedness, but does not by itself exclude two reduced components meeting in codimension two. The subsequent proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:product-Hasse-irred} supplies the missing irreducibility by mixed tacnodal unions and smooth points joining all restriction factors. It does not assume a generic symmetric-matrix rank bound for the special Cartier matrices.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [A pointed Cartier calculation] Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve in characteristic two with one-dimensional Cartier kernel, generated by $\omega$. If $P\in C$ satisfies $\omega(P)\ne0$, then Cartier induces a surjection \[ H^0(C,\omega_C(2P))\longrightarrow H^0(C,\omega_C), \] and its kernel is $k\omega$. If $D$ is ordinary, the corresponding map for $D$ is surjective with a one-dimensional kernel, whose nonzero members have a nonzero double-pole coefficient at $P$.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [Smoothness at a mixed tacnodal union] Let $X=E\times E$ be the fixed ordinary surface above. Let $C\in|L^a|$ and $D\in|L^e|$ be smooth curves without common components, ordinary except that $C$ has a one-dimensional Cartier kernel $k\omega$. Suppose they have a single simple tangency at $P$, are otherwise transverse, and $\omega(P)\ne0$. Then the full degree-$(a+e)$ Hasse divisor is smooth at $C\cup D$.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [The degree-one jet exception is small] On the fixed product, $L^e$ for $e\ge2$ separates second jets at one point and first jets at any two distinct points. For $L$ itself, second jets are separated at a point $P=(P_1,P_2)$ when neither $P_i$ is a flex in its plane cubic. For every $Q\ne P$, the joint first-jet evaluation has rank at least five; for fixed $P$, rank six fails only on the two fibres through $P$ and a finite set of other points.
depends_on: Self-contained proof in the indicated section
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [Uniform Hasse irreducibility] For the fixed surface and embedding, the degree-$d$ Hasse divisor is geometrically irreducible for every $d\ge4$.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [All full groups on the fixed ordinary product] Let $k$ be any perfect field of characteristic two, let \[ E:\ Y^2Z+XYZ+X^3+Z^3=0,\qquad X=E\times E,\qquad L=\mathcal O_E(3O)\boxtimes\mathcal O_E(3O), \] and use the fixed Segre embedding. For every $d\ge1$, the maximal relative Hasse--Witt rank is $r_d=9d^2-1$. On the smooth ordinary degree-$d$ hypersurface-section open, the entire geometric and arithmetic images coincide and are \[ G_{{\rm geom},d}=G_{{\rm arith},d}= \begin{cases} \GL_{9d^2-1}(\mathbf F_2),&d\text{ odd},\\[2mm] \left\{\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\0&I_3\end{pmatrix}: A\in\GL_{9d^2-4}(\mathbf F_2),\quad B\in M_{(9d^2-4)\times3}(\mathbf F_2)\right\},&d\text{ even}. \end{cases} \] In even degree this is exactly the pointwise stabilizer of all three independent invariant covectors, and its order is $2^{3(9d^2-4)}|\GL_{9d^2-4}(\mathbf F_2)|$. The representation is irreducible exactly in odd degree.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [A universal elliptic Cartier symmetrizer] Let $E:y^2+xy=x^3+A x^2+B$ over a perfect field of characteristic two, with $B\ne0$, and put $N=\mathcal O_E(3O)$. In the basis $(1,x,y)$ and with the Cartier-invariant differential $\eta=dx/x$, the root-removed Cartier multiplication matrix is \[ M(s)=\begin{pmatrix} s_0&B s_2&B s_1\\ s_2&s_1+A s_2&s_0+A s_1\\ 0&s_2&s_1+s_2 \end{pmatrix}. \] The constant invertible matrix \[ R=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&B\\0&0&B\\0&B&(1+A)B\end{pmatrix}, \qquad\det R=B^2, \] satisfies \[ RM(s)=\begin{pmatrix} s_0&0&B s_2\\ 0&B s_2&B(s_1+s_2)\\ B s_2&B(s_1+s_2)&B s_0+B s_1+(1+A)B s_2 \end{pmatrix}. \] Thus $RM(s)$ is symmetric and its diagonal is $R^t s$. For any pair of ordinary elliptic curves with degree-three line bundles, the analogous nine-dimensional Cartier pencil has a constant invertible symmetrizer and an invertible linear map to its nine diagonal entries.
depends_on: Self-contained proof in the indicated section
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [Squarefreeness from independent symmetric diagonals] Let $S(z)$ be an $m\times m$ symmetric matrix of linear forms in characteristic two, and suppose its diagonal entries are independent linear coordinates $z_1,\ldots,z_m$. Then $\det S$ is geometrically squarefree.

statement: [Jet bounds for arbitrary ordinary cubic factors] Let $X=E_1\times E_2$ with both elliptic curves ordinary in characteristic two and $L=\mathcal O_{E_1}(3O)\boxtimes \mathcal O_{E_2}(3O)$. The conclusions of Lemma~\ref{lem:product-small-degree-jets} hold on $X$. In addition, the singular-curve discriminant of $|L|$ is irreducible with a general one-node member, and its general member is ordinary.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [Uniform irreducible Hasse divisors on ordinary products] Let $E_1,E_2$ be arbitrary ordinary elliptic curves over a perfect field of characteristic two, and let $L=\mathcal O_{E_1}(3O)\boxtimes\mathcal O_{E_2}(3O)$. The full Hasse divisor in $|L|$ is geometrically reduced and has generic Cartier corank one on every component. For every $d\ge2$, the full Hasse divisor in $|L^d|$ is geometrically irreducible and reduced, with generic stable rank loss exactly one. Consequently the geometric relative Hasse--Witt group in degree $d\ge2$ is generated by transvections.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [An irreducible kernel for every ordinary pair] In the preceding theorem let $d\ge2$, put $b=9d^2$, and set $q=0$ for odd $d$ and $q=3$ for even $d$. The entire invariant-covector space has dimension $q$. Its common kernel $K\subset V_d$ is irreducible of dimension $b-1-q$, and $V_d$ has no invariant vector. The image on $K$ is irreducible and generated by transvections.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [An open locus of full degree-one images] There is a nonempty Zariski open subset $B^\circ$ of the space $B=\mathbf G_m^2$ of pairs \[ E_{b_i}:y^2+xy=x^3+b_i \] on which the geometric relative degree-one image for $\mathcal O(3O)\boxtimes\mathcal O(3O)$ is $\GL_8(\mathbf F_2)$.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [Ordinary nodal images under odd product isogenies] Let $\phi_i:E_i'\to E_i$ be odd-degree isogenies of ordinary elliptic curves in characteristic two, of degrees $m_i$, and put $\phi=\phi_1\times\phi_2$. For a general smooth ordinary $C'\in|\mathcal O_{E_1'}(3O)\boxtimes\mathcal O_{E_2'}(3O)|$, its image $C=\phi(C')$ is an ordinary nodal integral curve, $C'\to C$ is its normalization, and \[ \mathcal O_X(C)= \mathcal O_{E_1}(3m_2O)\boxtimes\mathcal O_{E_2}(3m_1O). \] Over a suitable dense open of the $C'$ parameter space, the permutation image on the nodes of $C$ is a subquotient of a product of copies of $S_{18}$.
