notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [A natural eight-dimensional block after an isogeny] Suppose the degree-one relative image on $E_1'\times E_2'$ is $\GL_8(\mathbf F_2)$, and let $\phi_i$ be as above. For every \[ d\ge \max(m_1,m_2)+1, \] the degree-$d$ geometric group on $E_1\times E_2$ contains an actual natural $\GL_8(\mathbf F_2)$ block fixing a complementary summand pointwise.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [Eventual full images for every ordinary pair] Let $E_1,E_2$ be any ordinary elliptic curves over a perfect field of characteristic two, with $L=\mathcal O_{E_1}(3O)\boxtimes\mathcal O_{E_2}(3O)$. There exist odd-degree isogenies $\phi_i:E_i'\to E_i$, of degrees $m_i$, such that for every $d\ge d_1=\max(m_1,m_2)+1$ the entire geometric and arithmetic images are \[ \begin{cases} \GL_{9d^2-1}(\mathbf F_2),&d\text{ odd},\\ \mathbf F_2^{3(9d^2-4)}\rtimes\GL_{9d^2-4}(\mathbf F_2), &d\text{ even}, \end{cases} \] where the second line is the full pointwise stabilizer of the three independent invariant covectors. The isogenies, and hence the displayed integer $d_1$, can be found by a terminating finite procedure over a finite field or an effectively presented finitely generated field of definition. No degree-one full-image assertion for an arbitrary pair is being inferred from the generic pair.

These are finite supporting calculations; the universal incidence assertions are proved in the preceding lemmas.

statement: [Explicit endomorphisms of every positive degree] For every integer $n\ge1$ there is an explicitly specified endomorphism $b:E_0\to E_0$ with $b^\dagger b=bb^\dagger=[n]$, where $\dagger$ is the Rosati involution for $\OO_{E_0}(O)$. In particular $\deg b=n$.

statement: [The ambient quotient and the even-degree obstruction] For every smooth $Y\in|N_m|$, $m\ge3$, its genus is $g=m^2+1$ and $\dim Q_Y=m^2-1$. Its $2$-rank $f_Y$ satisfies \[ f_Y\le m^2-1, \qquad f_Y\le m^2-3\quad\hbox{if }2\mid m. \] Moreover $\dim(Q_Y)_{\ss}=f_Y$.
notes: Exact hypotheses in statement; independent/targeted/computational audit distinctions are recorded in CHECK_EVENTS.tsv.

statement: [Exact generic rank in every hypersurface degree] For the specified $X\subset\mathbf P^8_{\mathbf F_2}$, the geometric generic stable rank in degree $d\ge1$ is \[ \boxed{\quad \dim E(Y,\OO_Y)_{\ss,\mathrm{gen}} =\begin{cases} 9d^2-1,&d\ \text{odd},\\ 9d^2-3,&d\ \text{even}. \end{cases}\quad} \tag{\dagger} \] The coherent relative space has dimension $9d^2-1$ in every degree. Consequently its generic Frobenius is bijective exactly for odd $d$. There is no integer $d_0$ making it generically bijective for every $d\ge d_0$. The generic stable rank is positive in every degree, so for this example the positivity threshold is exactly $d_0=1$.

statement: [An explicit nonreduced relative Hasse divisor] The relative coherent Frobenius bundle is $\mathcal E=\Omega^1_P$. Its determinant section, up to the constant trivialization implicit in the chosen basis, is \begin{equation} h(s)=D(s)^2Q(s),\qquad D(s)=\det S,\qquad Q(s)=s^{[2]t}Js. \end{equation} The cubic $D$ is geometrically irreducible; the cubic $Q$ is geometrically smooth and irreducible; they are distinct. Thus the relative Hasse divisor has a component of multiplicity two and a different component of multiplicity one. The generic relative stable rank is eight. A smooth generic section has genus ten and $2$-rank eight.

statement: [A first-derivative criterion for wild transvection inertia] Let $R=k[[t]]$ with $k$ algebraically closed of characteristic two, and let a rank-$r$ vector bundle over $R$ have regular semilinear Frobenius $F$. Suppose that its special fibre has stable rank $r-1$, its linearized kernel has dimension one, and its determinant has valuation one. Let $u$ generate the semilinear kernel in the special fibre, and let $v$ be the first derivative of $F(\widetilde u)$ at $t=0$, for a regular lift $\widetilde u$. If $v\notin ku$, the generic Lang local system has a nontrivial transvection in its inertia.

statement: [The geometric generic ordinary elliptic factor] Let $k=\mathbf F_2(t)^{\mathrm{perf}}$ be the perfect closure of the rational function field, and define \[ E_t:\ y^2+txy+y=x^3,\qquad E_0:\ y^2+y=x^3,\qquad X=E_t\times_k E_0, \qquad L=\OO_{E_t}(3O)\boxtimes\OO_{E_0}(3O). \] Use the cubic embeddings and the Segre map to embed $X$ in $\mathbf P^8_k$. The first elliptic factor is ordinary and the second is supersingular. For every $d\ge1$, the geometric generic relative stable rank is \[ \boxed{\quad \dim E(Y,\OO_Y)_{\ss,\mathrm{gen}} =\begin{cases} 9d^2-1,& d\ \text{odd},\\ 9d^2-2,& d\ \text{even}. \end{cases}\quad} \tag{\ddagger} \] The relative coherent dimension is always $9d^2-1$. Thus its generic Frobenius is bijective exactly in odd degree. The full generic curve defect $g(Y)-f_Y$ is one in odd degree and two in even degree. The same formulas hold after replacing $E_t$ by any elliptic curve over a perfect characteristic-two field whose $j$-invariant is transcendental over $\mathbf F_2$, and taking geometric generic ranks. This last assertion does not include arbitrary algebraic $j$-invariants.

statement: Let $(A,\Theta)$ be a principally polarized abelian variety of dimension $g$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic two, and let $L=\mathcal O_A(3\Theta)$ and $W=H^0(A,L)$. Then the diagonal coordinates are independent and $\det M(s)$ is a nonzero geometrically squarefree polynomial of degree $3^g$. In particular, for $g=2$ the degree-one full coherent Hasse divisor of $|3\Theta|$ is geometrically reduced and each of its components has generic linearized Cartier corank one.

statement: [Eventual exact images for all ordinary principally polarized surfaces] Let $(A,\Theta)$ be an ordinary principally polarized abelian surface over any perfect field $k$ of characteristic two, with a line bundle representing $\Theta$ over $k$, and embed it by $L=\mathcal O_A(3\Theta)$. After a finite extension of $k$, there exists an odd polarized isogeny $\phi:A'\to A$ with multiplier $n$ whose source has degree-one relative geometric group $\GL_8(\mathbf F_2)$. For the complete systems $|L^d|$, put $d_1=n+1$. For the ambient hypersurface systems of this fixed embedding, replace it by \[ d_1=\max\{n+1,\operatorname{reg}(\mathcal I_A)-1\}. \] For every $d\ge d_1$, put $r=9d^2-1$. If $d$ is odd, the entire geometric and arithmetic images both equal $\GL_r(\mathbf F_2)$. If $d$ is even, put $N=r-3$ and let $\Gamma\subset S_3$ be the actual Galois image permuting the three nonzero characters of $\ker F_A$. After compatible choices of bases the entire images are \[ G_{{\rm geom},d}= \left\{\begin{pmatrix}B&T\\0&I_3\end{pmatrix}: B\in\GL_N(\mathbf F_2),\ T\in M_{N\times3}(\mathbf F_2)\right\}, \] \[ G_{{\rm arith},d}= \left\{\begin{pmatrix}B&T\\0&\gamma\end{pmatrix}: B\in\GL_N(\mathbf F_2),\ T\in M_{N\times3}(\mathbf F_2),\ \gamma\in\Gamma\right\}, \] where $\Gamma$ acts by its three-dimensional permutation matrices. The representation is irreducible exactly in odd degree. The integer $n$, and hence the threshold, can be found by a terminating procedure over finite fields or effectively presented finitely generated fields of definition; over arbitrary perfect fields the statement gives existence without presupposing computable coefficients.
